page: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-amd is a cloud compute instance in the High Performance line, configured with an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provisions 4 vCPUs backed by 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core using a shared CPU allocation model. Memory capacity is set to 12.0 GB, delivering 3.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 260 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, one complimentary public IPv4 address, and supported instruction extensions such as AVX, AES, and SHA_NI, while omitting AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced compute results alongside constrained uncached memory throughput. In synthetic CPU workloads, stress-ng achieves 2427.57 on single-core and 9526.81 on multi-core operations, placing it in the middle tier. PassMark CPU scoring reaches 6640.94 with an encryption score of 3738.58. However, Geekbench metrics show lower throughput with a single-core score of 1110.0 and a multi-core score of 3485.0. While small-block cached memory bandwidth reaches 380.64 GB/sec, uncached 256 MB block read and write speeds are 24.31 GB/sec and 20.91 GB/sec respectively, reflecting lower-tier results in PassMark memory and database subtests.

With its shared CPU model and moderate uncached memory bandwidth, the instance is less suited for heavy database operations or sustained large-model data processing. Instead, the combination of 12.0 GB RAM and 260 GB NVMe storage provides a balanced operational base. The server is well aligned with workloads such as static web serving, intermediate application hosting, CI/CD testing pipelines, and staging environments.
description: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-amd is a general-purpose virtual instance in the High Performance family, featuring 4 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor at 2.0 GHz. It includes 12.0 GB of memory, 260 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, and a single public IPv4 address. Benchmark testing demonstrates mid-range computational capability in stress-ng and PassMark CPU routines, while uncached memory bandwidth and Geekbench scores fall into lower comparative percentiles. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES, and SHA_NI, though specialized vector engines like AVX-512 are absent. With its balanced core-to-memory ratio and fast onboard NVMe disk, this instance is appropriate for standard web serving, staging servers, and general development workloads.
